newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ex-tycoon Bernard Tapie gets new jail term.
newsitem.headline: French ex-tycoon Bernard Tapie gets new jail term.

text.p: A court on Friday sentenced imprisoned bankrupt French tycoon Bernard Tapie to an additional 18 months in jail with another 18 months suspended for embezzling funds from Marseille soccer club.
During Tapie's trial in May, a public prosecutor had urged the court in the Riviera port city of Marseille to jail the former soccer boss for two years, with another two years suspended.
Tapie, 54, was charged with embezzling 100 million francs ($17.5 million) when he was president of the Marseille club.

He stood trial, along with several other Marseille club officials, while serving an earlier jail sentence for fixing a match. The trial was repeatedly suspended when the former political boss and leftist cabinet minister suffered chest pains and breathing difficulties.

The Marseille court also convicted Alain Laroche, the club's former finance director, sentencing him to six months in jail with another 18 months suspended, and Jean-Pierre Bernes, Tapie's former right-hand man on the team, given a 30-month suspended sentence.
Former general manager Michel Hidalgo was handed a one-year suspended sentence while controller Elie Fellous was given a six-month prison term with another 18 months suspended.
